items.title: BI 248 Andrea Hiott: The Navigational Approach to the Mind
items.summary: Support the show to get full episodes, full archive, and join the Discord community.The Transmitter is an online publication that aims to deliver useful information, insights and tools to build bridges across neuroscience and advance research. Visit thetransmitter.org to explore the latest neuroscience news and perspectives, written by journalists and scientists.Read more about our partnership.Sign up for Brain Inspired email alerts to be notified every time a new Brain Inspired episode is released.To explore more neuroscience news and perspectives, visit thetransmitter.org.Andrea Hiott is a philosopher at Universität Heidelberg, but she has various degrees across philosophy and neuroscience. You may know her from her podcast Love and Philosophy, or her Way-making substack, or her writings elsewhere. Through all her work runs a central theme, that we need to go beyond dichotomous thinking and learn to hold paradoxes as they are. Holding Paradox is the title of her new book. The full title is Holding Paradox: The Navigational Approach to Mind, and that subtitle, the navigational approach, is the term Andrea uses for her version of what should replace the current computational metaphor of the mind. In the book, Andrea uses the rich history of research in a particular brain area, the hippocampus, to illustrate what holding paradox is and what the navigational approach is. The hippocampus is a good example to use, because it has two parallel histories- one as the seat of our memory, and another as a cognitive map, how we move through the world and how we move through our thoughts.Andrea's website. Book:Holding Paradox: The Navigational Approach to MindPodcast:Love and PhilosophySubstack:Way-makingRadical Embodied Relation at any Scale, from Remembering to Navigating.0:00 - Intro3:01 - Creating vs criticizing5:25 - Holding paradox9:04 - Neuroscience and philosophy11:42 - Hippocampus and movement18:05 - Computational metaphor30:52 - Ways of doing science43:25 - Why is now the time?51:34 - Navigational mind and AI1:09:27 - Perspectivalism vs holding paradox1:21:31 - Consciousness1:25:38 - How to be alive1:29:26 - Holding paradox community?
